1) Story file verification - Opened docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md and confirmed its contents match the specification provided in the prompt, including all Acceptance Criteria, Requirements (REQ-TEST-FIX-*), Implementation Notes, and Definition of Done checkboxes.
2) Implementation check – core rule - File: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts - Confirms existence of the ESLint rule implementing this story: - Rule options type `TestTraceabilityOptions` includes: - `autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean;` - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean;` - `testSupportsTemplate?: string;` matching the story’s Configuration Options. - `meta.fixable` is set to `"code"`, enabling ESLint `--fix` behavior. - JSON schema under `meta.schema` defines: - `autoFixTestTemplate` (boolean, default true) - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat` (boolean, default true) - `testSupportsTemplate` (string) - In `create(context)`: - Options destructured with defaults: `autoFixTestTemplate = true`, `autoFixTestPrefixFormat = true`, `testSupportsTemplate`. - Calls `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate })` to handle file‑level `@supports` template insertion. - Passes `autoFixTestPrefixFormat` and the constructed `describeRegex` into `handleCallExpression` so malformed `[REQ-...]` prefixes are normalized only when configured. - JSDoc traceability annotations for the rule explicitly map it to this story and requirements: - `@supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE`.
3) Implementation check – helper functions for templates and prefix fixes - File: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts
3.1) File-level `@supports` template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - `buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?: string)`: - Uses a default `baseTemplate` string when customTemplate is not provided: - `"@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ"`. - Builds a multi-line JSDoc comment: ``` /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ ``` - Provides clear TODO guidance and placeholder story path/REQ IDs, matching the story’s Template Examples and Template Quality / PLACEHOLDER requirements.
- `insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?)`: - Computes an insertion index, defaulting to 0. - If the source text starts with a shebang (`#!`), moves `insertIndex` to just after the first newline, so the shebang remains the first line (preserving executable semantics, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE and REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE). - Uses `fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment)` to insert the generated JSDoc comment, ensuring only a new comment is added and no code is altered.
- `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions)`: - Scans `sourceCode.getAllComments()` and checks if any contain `@supports` via regex `/@supports\b/`. - If at least one such comment exists, it does **nothing** – no template is added, avoiding duplicate or conflicting annotations. - If none exist, it reports `messageId: "missingFileSupports"` against a safe node (typically `Program`). - Provides a fixer **only** when `autoFixOptions.autoFixTestTemplate !== false`, returning a function that calls `insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, autoFixOptions.testSupportsTemplate)`. - Never attempts to infer the real story path or REQ IDs; it always uses the generic placeholder template or the user-supplied template string, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
3.2) REQ prefix format normalization (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - `normalizeReqId(raw: string)`: - `raw` is trimmed and uppercased. - Returns `null` unless the string begins with `"REQ"`, ensuring it only acts on recognizable REQ IDs. - Strips leading separators after `REQ` via `rest.replace(/^[-_\s:]+/, "")`. - Converts spaces and underscores to hyphens: `rest.replace(/[\s_]+/g, "-")`. - Collapses multiple hyphens into one: `rest.replace(/-+/g, "-")`. - Returns `"REQ-" + rest` when `rest` is non-empty. - This strictly normalizes an **existing** REQ ID, never creating a new base identifier and never inferring a requirement ID.
- `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): string | null`: - If the description already starts with a canonical prefix matching `/^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/`, it returns `null`, leaving correct prefixes unchanged. - Otherwise, attempts a square-bracket match: `/^\[\s*(REQ[^\]]*?)\s*](.*)$/i`. - If matched, it normalizes the captured REQ portion with `normalizeReqId` and reconstructs: `"[" + normalizedId + "]" + rest`. - If that fails, attempts a parenthesis match: `/^\(\s*(REQ[^)]*?)\s*\)(.*)$/i`. - If matched, also normalizes and converts to canonical bracket form: `"[" + normalizedId + "]" + rest`. - Returns `null` when no recognizable REQ‑based prefix is found, so no auto-fix is offered in ambiguous or non-REQ cases.
- `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode)`: - Reads the original literal text via `sourceCode.getText(originalNode)`. - Preserves the original quote style (single, double, or template literal) and escapes content appropriately. - Ensures only the string **content** is changed while preserving coding style, whitespace outside the literal, and surrounding code, aligning with REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE.
- `handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options)` (invoked by rule’s `CallExpression` handler): - Respects the `requireTestReqPrefix` and `autoFixTestPrefixFormat` options. - If the `description` does not start with a canonical `[REQ-...]` prefix, it: - Computes `normalizedDescription = normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description)` when `autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false`; else `normalizedDescription = null`. - Always reports `messageId: "missingReqPrefix"` to align with the validation story (020.0). - Supplies a fixer **only when** all are true: - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false`. - `normalizedDescription !== null` (i.e., an actual malformed REQ prefix was recognized and could be normalized safely). - The first argument is a literal string node. - The fixer uses `fixer.replaceText(literalNode, createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(literalNode, normalizedDescription, sourceCode))`. - This satisfies: - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT (spacing, delimiters, case, parentheses conversion). - REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE (only fixes clearly-identifiable REQ patterns; no guessing). - REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE (only string literal content is updated; structure and indentation remain unchanged). - REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE (never introduces a new prefix when none exists).
